description: Three Euclidean trigger sequencers driven from one clock, each with its own step count, density, rotation and clock division, plus outputs that hand the pattern from one track to another

params.text: Returns all three tracks to the start of their patterns and restarts the clock measurement
Divides or multiplies the clock for that track, from a quarter speed through the clock's own rate to four times it
Sets how many steps that track's pattern runs for, 1 to 32
Sets what share of that track's steps carry a hit, 0% to 100%, the hits spread as evenly through the pattern as the count allows
Rotates that track's pattern, up to 31 steps, moving where the hits fall without changing how many there are
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the length jack above it, -1 to +1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the fill jack above it, -1 to +1
Attenuates and inverts the voltage at the shift jack above it, -1 to +1

inputs.text: The clock every track counts; the interval between two edges here is the tempo the per-track dividers and multipliers work from
A rising edge returns all three tracks to the start of their patterns and restarts the clock measurement
Added to that track's LEN knob through the trimmer below it, one step per volt; the total is held between 1 and 32
Added to that track's FILL knob through the trimmer below it, 10% per volt; the total is held between 0% and 100%
Added to that track's SHFT knob through the trimmer below it, one step per volt; the total is held between 0 and one step short of the pattern length

outputs.text: A 10ms trigger at 10V on every step of that track that carries a hit
Goes to 10V whenever any of the three track outputs is high
Plays track 1 for one full pass of its pattern, then track 2 for one full pass, and repeats
Plays track 2 for one full pass of its pattern, then track 3 for one full pass, and repeats
Plays one full pass each of track 1, track 2, track 1 again and track 3, then repeats

notes: no track steps and the three chain outputs stay at 0V until a clock reaches CLK. The tempo is measured from the gap between clock edges, so the first edge after a reset produces nothing.
